            <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
                <div class="bg-gray-50 rounded-lg p-6 shadow-sm">
                    <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-800 mb-3">Error Code: E0 / F0 (Sensor Error)</h3>
                    <p class="text-md mb-4">Indicates a fault with a temperature sensor. This can lead to incorrect cooling or heating.</p>
                    <h4 class="font-semibold golden-text mb-2">Possible Solutions:</h4>
                    <ul class="list-disc list-inside text-sm space-y-1">
                        <li>Reset: Unplug the refrigerator for 5-10 minutes, then plug it back in. This often clears temporary sensor glitches.</li>
                        <li>Check Door Seals: Ensure the door is closing properly and the seals are intact. Warm air entering can confuse sensors.</li>
                        <li>Professional Help: If the error persists, a sensor replacement might be needed. Contact Atlas Aircon for expert diagnostics.</li>
                    </ul>
                </div>
                <div class="bg-gray-50 rounded-lg p-6 shadow-sm">
                    <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-800 mb-3">Error Code: dF / Cb (Defrost Sensor / Communication Error)</h3>
                    <p class="text-md mb-4">Relates to the defrost system or communication between control boards. Can cause frost buildup.</p>
                    <h4 class="font-semibold golden-text mb-2">Possible Solutions:</h4>
                    <ul class="list-disc list-inside text-sm space-y-1">
                        <li>Manual Defrost: Unplug the unit and empty it. Leave the doors open for 24-48 hours to fully defrost.</li>
                        <li>Check Vents: Ensure freezer and refrigerator vents aren’t blocked by food items.</li>
                        <li>Call an Expert: If manual defrost doesn’t help or the error returns quickly, components like the defrost heater, thermostat, or main control board might be faulty.</li>
                    </ul>
                </div>
                <div class="bg-gray-50 rounded-lg p-6 shadow-sm">
                    <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-800 mb-3">Error Code: ER CO / CO (Compressor Overload)</h3>
                    <p class="text-md mb-4">Often indicates the compressor is struggling or has failed. The fridge may not be cooling.</p>
                    <h4 class="font-semibold golden-text mb-2">Possible Solutions:</h4>
                    <ul class="list-disc list-inside text-sm space-y-1">
                        <li>Ventilation: Ensure adequate space around the refrigerator for air circulation.</li>
                        <li>Clean Coils: Dirty condenser coils can make the compressor work harder. Clean them if accessible.</li>
                        <li>Professional Repair: A persistent compressor error usually means the compressor itself, or its starting components, need replacement. This requires a professional fridge service Vadodara.</li>
                    </ul>
                </div>

                    <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-800 mb-3">Error Code: E r FF / FF (Freezer Fan Error)</h3>

                        <li>Expert Intervention: A replacement of the freezer fan motor is typically needed.</li>

                    <p class="text-md mb-4">The internal temperature has dropped below the set point, often due to a faulty thermostat or control board sending continuous cooling signals.</p>
